source_review.notes: Checked the primary RDD, MapReduce, and Dryad papers plus current official Spark, Flink, Tez, Beam, and Dask documentation. The sources support dependency width, co-partitioned joins, shuffle mechanics, adaptive skew/partition rewrites, exchange modes, keyed grouping, and graph terminology. All ten referenced URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed qualified parent partition set P, child set C, dependency relation E, parent fan-out, child fan-in, edge count, immediate recovery set R(c), byte function b(p,c), graph version V, and partitioner contract Q.
Checked set-builder directions and quantifiers in the narrow iff maximum parent fan-out is at most one and wide iff some parent fan-out exceeds one definitions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Parent fan-out and child fan-in remain explicitly distinct; multi-input partition identities are qualified by parent dataset.

evidence: Executed narrow-wide-dependency-relations with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced four, four, four, and twelve edges for the one-to-one, coalesce, aligned-join, and shuffle cases.
Recomputed maximum parent fan-out as one, one, one, and three; maximum child fan-in as one, two, two, and four; and all four c1 recovery-parent tuples.
Recomputed the exercise skew ratio as 600 GB divided by 8 GB equals 75 and the complete all-to-all surface as 50 times 100 equals 5,000 partition pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The fixture demonstrates exact finite relation calculations; it does not measure transport or production performance.

evidence: Derived narrowness by quantifying over each parent's dependent-child set, including the counterexample where child fan-in exceeds one under coalescing.
Derived aligned-join narrowness from two compatible qualified parent partitions feeding only the corresponding child and mixed join width when only one side repartitions.
Derived immediate and transitive recovery cones by following reverse dependency edges until valid durable materializations or source partitions.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Classification is relative to one realized physical relation and engine contract, while blocking, materialization, and barriers are separate properties.

evidence: Reviewed empty/sparse edges, one-to-one mapping, many-parent narrow coalesce, aligned and unaligned joins, mixed dependencies, all-to-all exchange, empty-block elision, broadcast, and barrier distinctions.

Reviewed zero/one/many target partitions, stale hash seeds and range boundaries, Unicode/case/null key differences, key-changing maps, hot keys, many-to-many join expansion, OOM, spill, fetch loss, speculative attempts, and executor loss.
Reviewed adaptive split/coalesce and join conversion, mixed exchange generations, threshold oscillation, broadcast expansion, regional loss, corrected identity links, and notification replay.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cost, movement, blocking, durability, scheduling coordination, and domain consequence are assessed independently.

evidence: Traced physical graph version, parent fan-out classification, partitioner compatibility, deterministic target ownership, accepted producer outcomes, and complete compatible consumer generation through exposition and exercises.
Checked that combination changes bytes without changing width and that adaptive rewrites change graph identity and retain old-to-new mappings.
Checked that recovery reuses only artifacts compatible in graph, input snapshot, code, schema, partitioner, and accepted attempt.
invariant_checking.notes: No operator name, partition number, function name, process success, or average metric is treated as sufficient proof.

evidence: Reviewed all ten classification and validation obligations from physical-plan selection through consequence review.

Checked counterexamples for child-fanin-equals-wide, every-join-wide, every-coalesce-narrow, combiner-makes-narrow, width-equals-blocking, narrow-equals-cheap, and partition-number-proves-compatibility claims.
Reviewed keyed routing, aligned join, exchange completion, generation fencing, recovery cut, skew diagnosis, and adaptive graph-version arguments.

evidence: Audited uses of iff, exactly one, every, compatible, complete, deterministic, accepted, safe, and prove.
Confirmed that the executable fixture is labeled as a finite relation demonstration rather than a benchmark or production correctness proof.
